findings.title: Central config (core/config.ini + get_default_options/apply_defaults) is dead: no consumer, and its values contradict the real defaults
findings.description: configurator.py presents itself as 'Central default options for hypertools' and a 'single source of truth' shared with datawrangler, and get_default_options/apply_defaults are exported from hypertools.core. But grep finds ZERO call sites outside hypertools/core itself, so editing core/config.ini changes nothing at runtime. Real runs confirm the values are stale fiction: [reduce] ndims=3 vs actual default full-rank (hyp.reduce on 180x4 data returned shape (180, 4)); [plot] linewidth=1 and style='.' vs actual matplotlib line linewidth 1.5 with no marker; [align] algorithm='hyper' vs actual signature default model='HyperAlign' with 'hyper' explicitly deprecated in align.py; [reduce] key is named 'algorithm' although the real kwarg is reduce=/model=; [cluster] n_clusters=3 merely coincides with the hardcoded signature default in cluster.py:135. Maintainers or advanced users editing config.ini get a silent no-op; the module docstring's claims are false in practice. Note: user-facing docs never mention this machinery, so end-user exposure is low, but the exported feature is broken as documented.
findings.repro:
cd /Users/jmanning/hypertools && grep -rn 'get_default_options\|apply_defaults' hypertools/ --include='*.py' | grep -v __pycache__ | grep -v 'core/configurator\|core/__init__\|bound_args'  # -> no consumers
MPLBACKEND=Agg .venv/bin/python -c "
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
np.random.seed(0); X = np.random.randn(180, 4)
print('reduce default shape:', np.asarray(hyp.reduce(X)).shape)  # config.ini says ndims=3
import matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
fig = hyp.plot(np.cumsum(np.random.randn(120, 8), axis=0))
print('linewidth:', fig.gca().get_lines()[0].get_linewidth())  # config.ini says 1
"
findings.expected: Either config.ini values drive the actual defaults (reduce -> 3 dims, linewidth 1), or the module/config should not claim to be the central defaults mechanism
findings.actual: reduce default shape: (180, 4)  [not 3 dims]; actual linewidth: 1.5 | config.ini [plot] claims linewidth=1; marker: None | config claims style='.'; grep shows zero consumers

findings.title: Config values are returned as raw strings ('3', 'False', '0.7') that are unusable as kwargs and truthy-dangerous
findings.description: hypertools' configurator calls dw.core.update_dict WITHOUT from_config=True, so no value is ever eval'd: apply_defaults('cluster') returns {'n_clusters': '3', 'verbose': 'False'} (all str). Feeding these to the intended targets fails (sklearn KMeans rejects n_clusters='3'), and bool('False') is True, so any truthiness check on verbose would invert the intent. Worse, the two config dialects are incompatible: dw's config.ini stores Python literals ('pandas' quoted, True, np.nan) designed for eval, while hypertools' config.ini stores bare tokens (mako, ., -, hyper), so passing hypertools sections through dw's from_config=True eval raises SyntaxError ([plot]) or NameError. If config.ini is ever wired up (see -001), every consumer would need per-value type coercion.
findings.repro:
MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
from hypertools.core import apply_defaults
import numpy as np
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
d = apply_defaults('cluster'); print(d, {k: type(v).__name__ for k, v in d.items()})
print('bool(verbose):', bool(d['verbose']))
KMeans(n_clusters=d['n_clusters']).fit(np.random.randn(50, 3))
"
findings.expected: Typed values (int 3, bool False, float 0.7) or documented string-only semantics with coercion helpers
findings.actual: {'n_clusters': '3', 'verbose': 'False'} {'n_clusters': 'str', 'verbose': 'str'}; bool(verbose): True; KMeans(n_clusters='3') -> InvalidParameterError : The 'n_clusters' parameter of KMeans must be an int in the range [1, inf). Got '3' instead. Also: dw.core.update_dict(dict(opts['plot']), {}, from_config=True) -> SyntaxError : invalid syntax (<string>, line 1)

findings.title: get_default_options(fname=) footguns: custom file silently REPLACES all hypertools defaults, nonexistent paths are silently ignored, sections are wholesale-replaced
findings.description: Passing fname merges dw's defaults with ONLY the given file -- hypertools' own config.ini is dropped entirely (after a custom fname, opts['plot'] is {}), so the documented way to load a custom config silently discards every [plot]/[reduce]/[align]/[cluster] default. A typo'd/nonexistent fname is silently ignored (configparser.read semantics) and returns dw-only defaults with no warning. Merging is a top-level section replacement, not a deep merge: a custom file's [impute] section with one key erases dw's 'model' key from that section. The returned dict also carries a 'DEFAULT' configparser artifact section and uneval'd dw expression strings such as \"os.path.join(os.path.expanduser('~'), '.datawrangler', 'data', '')\".
findings.repro:
MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
from hypertools.core import get_default_options
import tempfile, os
p = os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(), 'c.ini'); open(p, 'w').write('[impute]\\nextra_opt = 1\\n')
print('missing file:', sorted(get_default_options(fname='/nonexistent/x.ini').keys())[:3], '(no error)')
c = get_default_options(fname=p)
print('[plot] after custom fname:', c['plot'])
print('[impute] after custom fname:', c['impute'])
"
findings.expected: Custom file layered ON TOP of hypertools+dw defaults (or a documented replacement contract); FileNotFoundError (or warning) for a missing fname; deep per-option merge
findings.actual: hypertools [plot] survives with custom fname: GONE (only dw defaults + custom file merged); nonexistent fname: silently returned sections ... (no error raised); dw default [impute]: {'model': \"'IterativeImputer'\"} -> after custom-file [impute]: {'extra_opt': '1'} (model key kept? False)

findings.title: RobustDict semantics are internally inconsistent: .get() bypasses the default, .copy() silently drops it, and the mutable default is aliased across lookups
findings.description: rd['missing'] returns __default_value__ but rd.get('missing') returns None -- the two standard lookup idioms disagree. rd.copy() (dict.copy) returns a PLAIN dict that raises KeyError on missing keys, while copy.copy(rd) and pickle preserve RobustDict-ness -- so robustness silently disappears depending on which copy idiom is used. Because the same default object is returned for every missing key, mutating one result pollutes all future missing lookups (demonstrated: rd['missing1']['polluted']=True makes rd['missing2'] == {'polluted': True}); get_default_options() returns exactly this shape (__default_value__={}), so opts['nosection'].update(...) anywhere would corrupt later lookups on that opts object. Also asymmetric: the outer dict is forgiving but nested section dicts are plain (opts['plot']['nope'] raises KeyError).
findings.repro:
MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
from hypertools.core.shared import RobustDict
rd = RobustDict({'a': 1}, __default_value__={})
rd['missing1']['polluted'] = True
print(rd['missing2'], rd['missing1'] is rd['missing2'])
rd2 = RobustDict({'a': 1}, __default_value__='DV')
print(rd2['zzz'], rd2.get('zzz'))
print(type(rd2.copy()).__name__)
rd2.copy()['zzz']
"
findings.expected: .get() honors the default; .copy() returns a RobustDict; a fresh default (e.g. copy) per missing lookup, or a documented immutability requirement
findings.actual: {'polluted': True} True | rd2['zzz'] -> DEFAULT ; rd2.get('zzz') -> None | copy() type: dict, then KeyError: 'zzz'

findings.title: Custom exceptions are not importable from the top-level hypertools namespace and are undocumented user-facing
findings.description: A scientist wanting `except hypertools.HypertoolsIOError:` cannot: hasattr(hyp, 'HypertoolsError') and hasattr(hyp, 'HypertoolsIOError') are both False, and no docs/*.rst mentions any of the three exceptions (grep found zero matches). The only working paths are hypertools.core.exceptions (undocumented) and the hypertools._shared.exceptions shim (private-by-convention, and its own comment says it was 'Moved to hypertools.core.exceptions'). For a library whose loaders/backends deliberately raise these types, catching them precisely requires reading the source. Exporting the three exceptions from hypertools/__init__.py (and listing them in docs/api.rst) would make robust error handling discoverable.

print(hasattr(hyp, 'HypertoolsError'), hasattr(hyp, 'HypertoolsIOError'), hasattr(hyp, 'HypertoolsBackendError'))

findings.title: unpack_model silently ignores 'params' when both 'params' and 'kwargs' are present in a dict spec
findings.description: The legacy-dict translation only fires when 'args'/'kwargs' are absent. A user migrating from the legacy form who passes {'model': 'PCA', 'params': {'n_components': 4}, 'kwargs': {'n_components': 9}} gets NO DeprecationWarning and no error: 'params' is retained inertly in the resolved spec and ignored downstream while 'kwargs' wins -- their n_components=4 is silently dropped. Similarly, a dict without a 'model' key (e.g. the typo {'mdoel': 'PCA'}) passes through unchanged for downstream code to trip over, instead of failing fast with a clear message.
findings.repro:
MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -W error::DeprecationWarning -c "
from hypertools.core.shared import unpack_model
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
print(unpack_model({'model': 'PCA', 'params': {'n_components': 4}, 'kwargs': {'n_components': 9}}, valid=[PCA]))
print(unpack_model({'mdoel': 'PCA'}, valid=[PCA]))
"
findings.expected: A warning (or error) that 'params' conflicts with 'kwargs' and is being ignored; a clear error for dicts lacking a 'model' key
findings.actual: {'model': <class 'sklearn.decomposition._pca.PCA'>, 'params': {'n_components': 4}, 'kwargs': {'n_components': 9}, 'args': []} with no warning raised (-W error did not trip); {'mdoel': 'PCA'} passed through unchanged

findings.title: unpack_model error messages leak raw reprs (memory addresses) and give no guidance; class-vs-instance validation is asymmetric
findings.description: Invalid specs raise ValueError('unknown model: <__main__.NotAModel object at 0x100647d10>') -- a leaked default repr with a memory address, naming neither what kinds of spec are accepted nor (when valid= was provided) which names would have matched. Asymmetries make the contract hard to predict: unpack_model(PCA) (a class) with no parent_class raises ValueError, while the string 'PCA' and the instance PCA() both pass through unchanged in the same situation; unpack_model(None, parent_class=...) raises 'unknown model: None'.
findings.expected: Error names the offending spec, the accepted spec forms (string among valid names / class or instance of parent_class / dict with 'model'), e.g. 'NotAModel instance is not a BaseEstimator; pass a class/instance of ... or one of [...]'
findings.actual: 1: unknown model: <__main__.NotAModel object at 0x100647d10> | 2: unknown model: <class 'sklearn.decomposition._pca.PCA'> | 3: 'PCA' PCA()  (string and instance pass through where the class raised)

findings.title: hypertools.config is a misnomer holding only __version__, leaks importlib's 'version' function, and carries dead Python<3.8 fallback code
findings.description: The module named 'config' contains no configuration -- only __version__ -- while the actual config machinery lives in hypertools/core/configurator.py + config.ini; hypertools.config.version is the leaked importlib.metadata.version FUNCTION (prints as '<function version at 0x...>'), an attractive trap next to __version__. Its try/except falls back to 'from importlib_metadata import version' for 'Python < 3.8', but pyproject.toml requires-python >=3.10 and importlib_metadata is not a declared dependency, so the fallback is dead code that would ImportError anyway. Also, unlike dw's equivalent, there is no PackageNotFoundError fallback for running from an uninstalled source checkout (untested here; would require uninstalling hypertools).
findings.repro:
MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import hypertools.config as c
print([a for a in dir(c) if not a.startswith('_')])
print(c.version)
print(c.__version__)
"
findings.expected: Module exposes only __version__ (del version after use, or use 'from importlib.metadata import version as _version'); no <3.8 fallback in a >=3.10 package

findings.title: Default n_clusters differs by entry point: hyp.cluster() -> 3 but hyp.plot(cluster='KMeans') -> 5 (three competing default sources)
findings.description: Defaults for the same conceptual operation live in three places that disagree: cluster() signature n_clusters=3 (cluster/cluster.py:135), _shared/params.py parameters['KMeans'] n_clusters=5 (consumed by plot.py's cluster= path and text2mat), and the dead core/config.ini [cluster] n_clusters=3. Real run on identical 6-blob data: hyp.cluster(X, cluster='KMeans') yields 3 unique labels while hyp.plot(X, '.', cluster='KMeans') colors 5 clusters. A scientist cross-checking their plot against hyp.cluster labels gets different partitions without any parameter change. ('defaults sane' mandate; root cause is core-level default duplication, though the fix likely touches plot.py/params.py.)
findings.expected: Same default k for the same spec on both entry points
findings.actual: hyp.cluster(X) unique labels: 3 | hyp.plot(X, '.', cluster='KMeans') distinct colors: 5 | hyp.cluster(X, cluster='KMeans') unique labels: 3

findings.title: set_interactive_backend accepts an invalid backend name silently; HypertoolsBackendError only surfaces at the first interactive plot
findings.description: hyp.set_interactive_backend('bogus_backend_xyz') returns without complaint; the HypertoolsBackendError ('Failed to switch the plotting backend to ... You may be missing required dependencies, or this backend may not be available for your system', chained from ModuleNotFoundError) only appears when the first interactive/animated plot runs -- typically far from the misconfiguration site in a script. The deferred message itself is clear and correctly typed (isinstance HypertoolsError True). Fail-fast validation (or a warning) at set time would localize the mistake. (Overlaps the plot-backend unit; recorded here because this is the primary raiser of the core HypertoolsBackendError.)
findings.repro:
MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
hyp.set_interactive_backend('bogus_backend_xyz')  # no error here
print('set silently OK')
hyp.plot(np.random.randn(30, 3), interactive=True)
"
findings.expected: Immediate error/warning naming the unknown backend at set time
findings.actual: set silently OK; then on plot: HypertoolsBackendError : Failed to switch the plotting backend to bogus_backend_xyz. You may be missing required dependencies, or this backend may not be available for your system

findings.title: shared.get() returns the ENTIRE list for out-of-range and negative indices
findings.description: get([10,20,30], 5) and get([10,20,30], -1) both return [10, 20, 30]. The out-of-range fallback is documented ('if in range, else value itself') and supports the one-shared-parameter idiom, but it means a per-dataset parameter list that is shorter than the dataset count silently hands LATER datasets the whole list as their parameter instead of erroring, and a negative index -- valid on every other Python sequence -- silently returns the list too. A length mismatch warning (or supporting negative indices) would prevent silent parameter misassignment in manipulators.
findings.repro:
MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
from hypertools.core.shared import get
print(get([10, 20, 30], 5), get([10, 20, 30], -1))
"
findings.expected: Error/warning on out-of-range per-dataset parameter lists; Python-conventional negative indexing (or an explicit error)

findings.title: hypertools.core export surface is inconsistent: shared helpers RobustDict/unpack_model/get exported but is_reused_pipeline is not; bare 'get' is a collision-prone name
findings.description: hypertools/core/__init__.py re-exports RobustDict, unpack_model and the very generically named 'get' from core.shared, but not is_reused_pipeline (ImportError: cannot import name 'is_reused_pipeline' from 'hypertools.core'), which dispatchers import from core.shared directly. Either all shared helpers are internal (export none) or the surface should be complete; exporting a function named simply 'get' invites shadowing bugs in 'from hypertools.core import *'-style usage.
findings.repro:
MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
from hypertools.core import get, RobustDict, unpack_model  # OK
from hypertools.core import is_reused_pipeline  # ImportError
"
findings.expected: Consistent, deliberate export list (and a more specific name than 'get' if it stays public)
